doc.title: Artie Shaw — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

chapter: After the war: analysis and the last bands
title: The Musicraft band and the collapse of the band business; the 1949 band
summary: He went out with the Musicraft band, says the band business was impossible, and calls the 1949 bop-oriented band his worst period.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Quitting the band: why sidemen left

blocks.x: Then I’d go out on the road. Then I went out on the road with a band. It was fine. That was that Kitty Kallen, Jerry . . .
Yeah, and there were some good records. But how many times can you do that?
What was the . . . This was at a time when we read that the band business was getting tougher.
Oh, it was impossible. There’s no band business anywhere. People say, “The big bands are coming back.” I say, “Yeah, next football season.”
At that time of the Musicraft band, things were getting tougher then, right?
Yeah. It was very difficult. Also, in ’49, when I had the last big band I ever had, which is shortly after that, that was the worst period I’ve ever been in. The audience loathed that band.
